findings.description: Target 06 separately encoded Loeb's recognition of something undesirable or strange and his concluding recognition of the desirability of following instrumental reasons, duplicating one conclusion as two contact units.

Move 09 directly answers Lutz's immediately preceding claim that wishful thinking and the gambler's fallacy are not ways of getting knowledge, not his earlier general account of a priori knowledge locked by the reviewed inventory.

Once move 09 is paired with its immediate target, it attacks the desire-relative account's ability to ground criticism but does not attack whether a priori knowledge is analytic, so the analytic-a-priori bridge was ineligible.

The repaired move 11 remains an eligible opponent-responsive act in chronological quarter four, and the full inventory retains exactly two responsive acts per quarter and the required side and mode counts.
Enoch explicitly cedes the pro closing time to Eric Sampson, whose sustained argumentative voice owns move 11 through the subsequent moderator transition; pro-side ownership is high confidence.
The move 11 boundary isolates Sampson's single self-undermining objection and excludes the preceding epistemology recap and following elaboration, so it is one atomic single-speaker act.

Lutz's exact prior evidential-connection principle is a genuine skeptical constraint attacked by Sampson's self-undermining objection, and its one indispensable condition is neither omitted nor duplicated.

Move 11 attacks only the con route's subsidiary evidential-connection bridge; it neither completes the anti-realist motion nor independently contacts the con route's analytic-a-priori bridge within the locked atomic excerpt.

The full caption chain, all twelve move spans and excerpts, all eight prior opponent targets, their digests, chronological order, semantic claims, and source limitations were independently rechecked with no remaining source-fidelity violation.
